text.p: Portugal's biggest retail and real estate group Sonae Investimentos said on Monday it posted a 60 percent year-on-year increase in net profit after minority interests to 20.7 billion escudos ($122 million).
Sonae Investimentos reported a 26 percent year-on-year increase in turnover to 451 billion escudos. Total cash flow rose by 32 percent to 42.7 billion escudos.
The group said it would propose to a shareholders' general assembly a 1996 gross dividend of 150 escudos per share, unchanged from 1995.
"During 1996 Sonae Investimentos maintained the strong rate of expansion that has allowed it to practically double its consolidated turnover over the past three years," Sonae said in a statement.

"Sonae's 26 percent growth in sales in 1996 reflected the inclusion for the first time of its retail activities in Brazil, the moderate increase in its distribution activities in Portugal and the stable contribution from Sonae Industria," it added.
"The expansion in 1996 was essentially organic, supported by the maintenance of a high level of investment," it said.
Wood products unit Sonae Industria reported a 1996 consolidated net profit after minority interests of 0.45 billion escudos, down from 1.09 billion in 1995.
Sonae Investimentos said it expected to report a 15 to 20 percent increase in sales in 1997, compared with 1996.

"We are expecting an increase in turnover of between 15 and 20 percent, supported by a higher rate of growth of distribution activities in Portugal and Brazil and the impact of new business in specialised retail activity," it said.
Sonae Investimentos posted a 12.2 percent year-on-year increase in its extraordinary profits, mainly due to gains from its real estate arm Sonae Imobiliaria.
Sonae Investimento shares were down 73 escudos to 5,450 escudos in light volume of 37,330 shares in mid-afternoon trade on Lisbon bourse.
